title: A Joyful Song of Thanks
overview: A short song calling the whole world to come gladly before God, because he made his people, cares for them, and his love and faithfulness never run out.

parts.label: A call to every land (vv. 1-2)
parts.note: The psalm invites not just Israel but people everywhere to cheer for the LORD, like a crowd greeting a king. Worship here is meant to be glad and full of song, not a grim duty.

parts.label: Made by God, belonging to him (v. 3a)
parts.note: The reason for joy is that the LORD alone is God, and he made his people, so they belong to him. Ancient copies differ by one Hebrew letter here, so some read "and not we ourselves" while others read "and we are his."

parts.label: Sheep of his pasture (v. 3b)
parts.note: In the ancient world kings were often pictured as shepherds, and here God is the shepherd who owns and feeds his flock. The image joins belonging with being looked after.

parts.label: Entering the temple (v. 4)
parts.note: The gates and courts are the entrance and open courtyards of the temple in Jerusalem, where ordinary worshippers gathered. The Hebrew heading links the psalm to giving thanks, and many scholars think it was sung as people walked in, perhaps bringing a thank offering, though no one can be sure.

parts.label: The reason to give thanks (v. 5)
parts.note: The song ends by naming why: God is good, his love lasts forever, and his faithfulness carries on through every generation. The Hebrew word for love here means steady, loyal love, the kind that keeps a promise.

think: Is gratitude something a person can choose, or does it only come when life already feels good?
